faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following recommended color correction methods:
Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.
Compare the print result with the image on your computer screen in a well-lit environment. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

If there are no gaps in the nozzle check pattern, try the solutions below.
Horizontal Banding
Increase the print resolution.
Turn off
Simple Settings
and uncheck the
High Speed
setting in the printer driver.
Select an alternate paper profile for ink coverage.
Select the correct paper type in the printer driver.
Adjust the paper feed
Vertical Banding
Turn off
Simple Settings
and uncheck the
High Speed
setting in the printer driver.
Align the print head.

faqs.answer: EPSON does not recommend refilling ink cartridges. Refilled cartridges can cause print quality problems. In the printer's User's Guide, we advise "Use only genuine EPSON ink cartridges and do not refill them. Other products may cause damage not covered by EPSON's warranty".

faqs.question: I see the message Communication Error when I use a USB connection. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Delete all print jobs in the print queue.
Turn the printer off.
Note:
Make sure the USB cable is connected correctly.
Restart your computer. When the desktop appears, turn your printer on and follow the on-screen instructions.
Note:
If the problem continues, turn the printer off again and delete the printer in the list of printers. Then disconnect the USB cable from the printer and connect it again.

faqs.question: An ink out light is flashing on the front panel. What does this mean?
faqs.answer: If one of these lights is flashing (which indicates there is approximately 5% of the ink left in the corresponding cartridge), the ink supply is getting very low and will need to be replaced shortly.  If one of the ink lights is on but not flashing, the corresponding cartridge is empty and you need to replace it to continue printing.

faqs.question: Will using non-Epson inks in my product void my warranty?
faqs.answer: Epson does not recommend refilling or using 3rd party ink cartridges. Using these products will not void the product's original warranty, however, if these 3rd party products cause a failure, the repair of that failure will not be covered under warranty.

faqs.question: Are the ink cartridges refillable?
faqs.answer: EPSON does not recommend refilling ink cartridges. Refilled cartridges can cause print quality problems. In the printer's User's Guide, we advise "Use only genuine EPSON ink cartridges and do not refill them. Other products may cause damage not covered by EPSON's warranty".

faqs.question: My product needs repair. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Your product has been discontinued for more than eight years.  Replacement parts are very limited which makes repair nearly impossible.  We highly recommend replacing your product with a newer model.

faqs.question: My nozzle patterns have missing gaps in two colors. How many cleaning cycles do I need to run?
faqs.answer: Run the nozzle check utility in the standard Epson driver. You may need to run as many as 7 cleaning cycles with a nozzle check in between to completely clean the print head. If you still see gaps in the pattern, contact Epson's technical support for further assistance.

faqs.question: How often should I run cleaning cycles?
faqs.answer: Cleaning cycles are necessary only if you see horizontal or vertical banding in your printouts. They may also improve print quality if your documents are faint, the colors are incorrect, or colors are missing. You can periodically print a nozzle check pattern to ensure the print head and printer are functioning properly. Also turn on the printer at least once a month to keep the nozzles clean.

faqs.question: How should I align the print head?
faqs.answer: Use the Print Head Alignment utility in the standard Epson driver. To start this utility, click the Utility tab or button in the printer software window and click Print Head Alignment. Repeat the alignment at least three times to ensure the greatest accuracy. Run the utility whenever you see vertical banding lines or skewed characters.

faqs.question: What is the thickest paper that can be used in my product?
faqs.answer: The cassette tray accepts paper up to .43 mm thick and professional proofing paper up to 52 lbs.  The rear manual feed slot, which feeds paper straight through the printer, accepts paper up to 200 lbs.

faqs.question: Can I use any type media and expect my prints to last up to 200 years?
faqs.answer: Only media listed in the Printer Guide that is designed for the archival inks can last up to 200 years, if stored properly.  Epson does not guarantee the longevity of any prints.

faqs.question: Can I use the same paper on the Pro 5500 that I used on my Pro 5000?
faqs.answer:
Some media can be used on both printers and other media maybe designed only for the Pro 5000 or Pro 5500.  Please see the
Printer Guide
for a list of media recommended for the Pro 5500.

faqs.question: Why does my product make a grinding noise when I load paper?
faqs.answer:
Check to see if the Paper Out light is flashing, indicating there's paper jammed inside the printer. If there is a jam see
Clear paper jams
in the Printer Guide. If grinding occurs from the front and rear and there's no sign of a paper jam, contact Epson's technical support for further assistance.

faqs.question: How long will my prints last on the media designed for the Pro 5500?
faqs.answer: With the state-of-the-art Epson Archival Ink technology, the Pro 5500 produces prints with a lightfastness rating up to 200 years.  This rating is based on accelerated testing of prints on specialty media, displayed indoors, under glass.

faqs.question: My prints were coming out fine, but now I'm getting a color shift.
faqs.answer: First, print the nozzle pattern from the non-postscript driver in the Utility folder to make sure there are no gaps in the pattern or any colors missing completely. If the nozzle pattern is not complete, then run some cleaning cycles making sure to print the nozzle pattern after each cleaning. Also if using a 3rd party paper, try one of the Epson papers designed for the Pro 5500 printer, making sure to select the appropriate media setting in the driver.

faqs.question: My printout has lines running through it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
First, check your driver settings and make sure the media type setting matches your paper type and that the appropriate print quality (resolution) is selected for your document. If the settings are correct, make sure your paper is loaded with the printable side facing the correct way. In the tray or front manual feed slot, load paper face-down. In the rear manual feed slot, load paper face-up.
If you still see banding, print a nozzle check pattern from the utility menu in the driver. Each staggered horizontal and straight vertical line should be complete, with no gaps in the dot pattern. If there are any gaps in the nozzle pattern, run a cleaning / nozzle pattern cycle. You may need to run up to 7 cleaning /nozzle pattern cycles to completely clean the print heads. If the nozzle pattern prints correctly, then run the printhead alignment utility using Epson coated paper and check it for misalignment with a loupe.

faqs.question: How do I check the default IP address on the optional C12C823912 EpsonNet Internal Print Server 2 (10 Base T / 100 Base TX)?
faqs.answer: You can check it by pressing the Status Sheet button on the adapter for about three seconds on the adapter.  This private IP address may cause a conflict on your network.  Ask your system administrator for a valid IP address that is within your subnet so it doesn't conflict with any other device.

faqs.question: Can my product's memory be easily cleared?
faqs.answer: Yes. Turn off the printer, wait 20 seconds, and then turn it back on.

faqs.question: Can I connect my product to a network?
faqs.answer: You can attach the printer to almost any Mac or PC network by installing the optional C12C823912 EpsonNet Internal Print Server 2 (10 Base T / 100 Base TX) Type B interface card into the printer's Type B interface slot. The print server automatically detects the network speed for operation at 10MB or 100MB per second.

faqs.question: If the media I am using is not an option on the driver, which setting should I use?
faqs.answer: If you're using Epson paper, the instruction sheet included with the paper may indicate which paper setting to use. If you're using non-Epson paper, Epson recommends contacting the paper manufacturer for the recommended setting. You may need to experiment with the different settings to determine which one is best for your paper.

faqs.question: How many total pages can my product print in its life cycle?
faqs.answer: The printer is rated at 75,000 total print volume for letter size pages only. Printing on larger paper, like Super A3/B size, reduces the total print volume.

faqs.question: What are the options for connecting my product?
faqs.answer: The printer comes with both a USB and parallel printer port. It includes a Type-B interface card slot for adding an optional Firewire or Ethernet adapter. The multi-protocol Ethernet adapter connects the printer to almost any network through a network hub or switch. The FireWire adapter lets you connect to both Mac and PC FireWire-compatible systems for data rates up to 400MB per second.

faqs.question: How do I know when my product is receiving information?
faqs.answer: The printer's Power light flashes when it's receiving data.

faqs.question: Which connection provides the fastest throughput on my Mac or PC system?
faqs.answer: FireWire technology provides the fastest throughput. It communicates with external peripherals at up to 400MB per second.  A USB connection provides the second fastest throughput and an Ethernet connection is the third fastest. A parallel connection on a PC system is the slowest.

faqs.question: My product is running slowly. What should I do?
faqs.answer: If the printer hesitates after each pass of the print head, the system may not be able to process the file fast enough to keep the printer running at full speed. If you're using a PC with a parallel connection to the printer, try connecting with a USB cable instead. This increases the data transfer rate to 12MB per second.  Also check your system resources and turn off any unnecessary programs that may be running in the background. If you're using a Mac, also turn off all other programs and try printing again with background printing off.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.
